title: FTC Issues 50 Page Subpoenas to OpenAI and Anthropic over AI Safety
summary:
Consumer protection violations are the primary focus of a new regulatory investigation into the safety protocols of leading artificial intelligence developers. The Federal Trade Commission issued civil subpoenas on Wednesday to OpenAI and Anthropic, each exceeding 50 pages, demanding records on internal safeguards, privacy policies and marketing materials in response to recent safety lapses.

The agency also plans to compel testimony from top AI executives and request information from third-party organizations. On the same day, eight US states—Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska and West Virginia—separately sued OpenAI, alleging the company misled consumers about the safety of ChatGPT, particularly for children.

🚨Holy Moly. The FTC has sent OpenAI and Anthropic civil subpoenas more than 50 pages long each, demanding documents on AI safety incidents, internal safeguards, marketing materials and privacy policies, Axios reports.

The investigation focuses on potential consumer protection violations. The agency also plans to compel top AI executives to testify and send additional investigative demands to third-party AI organizations.

On the same day, eight US states separately sued OpenAI, alleging it misled consumers about ChatGPT's safety, particularly for children.

The states are Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana.
